t.E635.agn: In 1974 JECFA set an ADI 'not specified' for this mixture. In JECFA's 1974 evaluation it was reported that intake of large amounts of these compounds in humans may increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion, and that this should be taken into account for people predisposed to gout and for those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion.
t.E635.body: A mixture of inosine and guanosine 5'-monophosphates; these nucleotides occur naturally in all tissues and are broken down to uric acid in humans.
t.E635.eff.0.t: May increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion
t.E635.eff.0.w: People predisposed to gout and those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion
t.E635.eval: May be of animal (meat/fish) or fermentation origin; the source may not be stated.
t.E635.prod: Produced by microbial fermentation or by breaking down RNA obtained from yeast.
t.E635.regx.1: In the E 626–635 ribonucleotides group; authorised at quantum satis in salt substitutes and seasonings/spice blends.
t.E635.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was published in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E635.summary: A mixture of disodium guanylate and inosinate (I+G); a flavour enhancer. Common in instant soups, crisps and noodle seasonings.
t.E635.what: A flavour enhancer that, as a mixture of inosinate and guanylate, strengthens meaty (umami) taste.
